newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China talking with foreign firms on mineral mining.
newsitem.headline: China talking with foreign firms on mineral mining.

text.p: China is negotiating contracts for risk exploration and mining for gold and diamonds with a number of foreign companies, an official of Beijing's Ministry of Geology and Mineral Resources said on Monday.

The deputy director of the Ministry's bureau of geological service and mineral resouces, Professor Zhang Hongtao, said the companies included Australia's Broken Hill Proprietary, Canada's Barrick Gold, Newmont Mining of the United States and South Africa's De Beers.
"We are very busy with the discussions," Zhang told Reuters while attending the three-day Asian Gold Congress in Hong Kong.
The bureau was putting the finishing touches to procedural outlines which would allow foreign firms mining and exploration rights in China, he said.
China announced early this month long-awaited amendments to its mineral resources law which would give foreign companies mining rights on Chinese soil.
"The details should be ready by the beginning of 1997," Zhang said.

He said many foreign companies were interested in the potentially huge deposits surrounding one of China's largest gold mines, the 26-sq-km (10 sq miles) Sawayaerdun in northwestern Xinjiang province.
